validity.recommendation: Keep the row. It is a real, well-documented cross-border gas transmission line, not a duplicate. Apply the minor fixes below: correct SegmentCost 195M->190M, set the Iranian owner to National Iranian Gas Company (NIGC) rather than 'Iran Ministry of Petroleum', and fix the route Start/End fields from the placeholder 'Asia' to Korpeje / Kordkuy.
validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: solid. The Korpeje-Kordkuy (Korpeje-Kurtkui / Korpezhe-Kord Kuy) line is Turkmenistan's first gas export pipeline to Iran, inaugurated 29 Dec 1997 by presidents Niyazov and Khatami. Confirmed by multiple INDEPENDENT origins that do NOT trace to GEM: Turkmen state media orient.tm (states 197 km, 132 km in Turkmenistan, opened Dec 1997) and two separate Jamestown Foundation articles (1998 inauguration; 2022 debt/reopening piece). GEM's own cited sources (Wikipedia, mfa.gov.tm, BBC 1997 blast report, Olcott book chapter) also support it. CLASSIFICATION: correct -- an international gas TRANSMISSION trunk, not gathering/process/oil. DUPLICATE: none. Distinct from P0748 (Hajiqabul-Astara-Abadan), P0742 (Dauletabad-Sarakhs-Khangiran, the other TM->Iran line via Khangiran), and P5984 (Rasht-Chelavend). GulfPub carries a separate 'Korpezhe - Kord Kuy | Operating | International | Korpezhe, Turkmenistan -> Kord Kuy, Iran | op=Turkmengaz dia=40.0 len_km=120' record -- that is the SAME pipe (confirms it), and its len_km=120 is the 120-MILE figure mis-scraped as km (=~197-200 km), so it is not a real length disagreement. ATTRIBUTION: Turkmengaz confirmed as owner/operator on the Turkmen side (GulfPub + Jamestown). On the Iranian side GEM lists 'Iran Ministry of Petroleum'; the 2022 Jamestown piece says the line 'was owned and operated by state monopoly Turkmengaz and the National Iranian Gas Company (NIGC)' -- NIGC (a subsidiary of the Ministry) is the more precise Iranian party; minor caveat. SPEC: Length 197 km matches orient.tm EXACTLY (Wikipedia rounds to 200 km = 135 TM + 65 IR; orient.tm gives 197 km / 132 TM). Capacity 8 bcm/y corroborated by both Jamestown articles + orient.tm -- solid. StartYear 1997 solid. Diameter 1000 mm (39 in) supported only by GEM's Wikipedia source (GulfPub says 40 in / 1016 mm -- consistent to rounding) -- medium confidence, no strong independent confirmation. FuelSource 'Korpeje and Gamyshlydzha fields' -- Korpeje field confirmed; Gamyshlydzha unverified independently (medium). SegmentCost: GEM shows US$195,000,000 but every independent source (Jamestown 2022, Wikipedia) says US$190 million -- recommend correcting to 190M (spec caveat). STATUS: 'operating' is defensible NOW but has history -- the line was long-dormant after Iran/Turkmen supply was suspended in early 2017 over a payment dispute; flows resumed ~2023 via swap arrangements (Jamestown 2022 describes the debt-clearing reopening deal). Worth a ResearcherNotes line on the 2017-2023 dormancy.

fills.researcher_notes: orient.tm (Turkmen state media): 'Its length from the Turkmen gas field of Korpeje to the Iranian city of Kurtkui is 197 kilometers, of which 132 kilometers run through the territory of Turkmenistan.' Matches GEM's 197 km exactly.
Jamestown 2022: 'With an annual capacity of 8 billion cubic meters (bcm)'. Jamestown 1998 inauguration piece and orient.tm both give 8 bcm/y. Two+ independent origins agree with GEM's 8.00 bcm/y.

Jamestown 2022: 'opened in December 1997'. orient.tm: 'The opening of the Korpedje-Kurtkui gas pipeline took place in December 1997.' Two independent origins confirm StartYear 1997 (inaugurated 29 Dec 1997).

orient.tm names both endpoints: 'from the Turkmen gas field of Korpeje to the Iranian city of Kurtkui' (Kurtkui = Kordkuy, in Golestan province). Corroborated by GulfPub ('Korpezhe, Turkmenistan -> Kord Kuy, Iran').

Jamestown 2022: the line 'was owned and operated by state monopoly Turkmengaz and the National Iranian Gas Company (NIGC).' GulfPub also lists op=Turkmengaz. Suggests changing GEM's Owner2 from the vaguer 'Iran Ministry of Petroleum' to NIGC (the operating subsidiary). Single strong source for the NIGC refinement -> medium.

routes.start_name: Korpeje (Korpedzhe) gas field, Balkan Province, western Turkmenistan (north of Okarem/Ekerem)
routes.end_name: Kordkuy (Kord Kuy / Kurtkui), Golestan Province, Iran
routes.corridor_desc: The line runs ~197 km from the Korpeje field in southwestern Turkmenistan (Balkan Province), of which ~132 km are inside Turkmenistan, generally southward/southwestward down the southeastern Caspian coastal plain, crosses into Iran and terminates at the city of Kordkuy in Golestan province (near Gorgan, just inland from the southeastern Caspian shore). Endpoints are well-established named cities/fields; the Kordkuy terminus coordinate is confident, the Korpeje field coordinate is APPROXIMATE (a real named field north of Okarem but I could not source an exact decimal coordinate -- treat +/- a few tens of km). No precise waypoints sourced.
routes.researcher_notes: Endpoints established from orient.tm (Korpeje field -> Kurtkui/Kordkuy) and corroborated by GulfPub. NOTE the sheet's route Start/End fields currently read the placeholder 'Asia' -- they should be Korpeje and Kordkuy; the underlying QGIS geometry (RouteNotes: 'NF 8/29/24: Mapped with QGIS') is presumably correct so RouteAccuracy 'high' is defensible, but the human-readable Start/End labels need fixing. Kordkuy coordinate (36.7897N, 54.1075E) is the known city location; Korpeje field coordinate (~38.45N, ~54.35E) is APPROXIMATE from the named field north of Okarem -- not a precise/fabricated value, flagged as loose. No coordinates invented.

summary: P0749 Korpeje-Kordkuy confirmed real, correctly classified international gas transmission trunk, not a duplicate; verdict confirmed (caveat) with minor fixes: cost 195M->190M, Iranian owner -> NIGC, route Start/End 'Asia' -> Korpeje/Kordkuy, note 2017-2023 dormancy.
